title: Worker repeatedly fails and requeues valid ticket event
customer_impact: Ticket creation remains available, but the affected ticket stays in queued processing state while the live worker repeatedly receives and fails the same valid durable event.
scope: RabbitMQ broker, API, PostgreSQL connectivity, Redis, and the worker consumer remain healthy. The fault is ticket-scoped to the worker's processing update and produces repeated nack/requeue cycles for one valid message.

timeline.event: A controlled ticket-scoped PostgreSQL trigger began rejecting the worker's processed-state update while all services and the RabbitMQ consumer remained online.
L2 acknowledged the P2 asynchronous processing degradation and correlated the affected ticket request ID through repeated worker job_failed events.
RabbitMQ still reported one consumer and retained the message in ready/unacknowledged state while the ticket remained processing_status=queued.
API readiness, queue-health, PostgreSQL SELECT 1, Redis PING, and RabbitMQ diagnostics remained healthy, rejecting broker, consumer-loss, and broad dependency-outage hypotheses.
The controlled transient processing condition was disabled without restarting worker, API, RabbitMQ, PostgreSQL, or Redis.
The same consumer retried the same request successfully, the original ticket became processed, and queue depth returned to zero.

evidence: healthy baseline with one RabbitMQ consumer and completed ticket processing
incident ticket remained processing_status=queued while the fault was active
same request ID produced at least three correlated worker job_failed events
worker job_failed log included the controlled processing exception
RabbitMQ consumer count remained one during the incident
the failing message remained in ready or unacknowledged queue state during retries
API readiness and queue-health remained HTTP 200
PostgreSQL SELECT 1 and Redis PING remained successful
worker and API container identities remained unchanged
after clearing only the transient processing condition, the same request produced one job_completed event
queue returned to zero messages and the original ticket became processed
resolution: L2 isolated the issue to repeated worker processing failures rather than consumer loss or broker outage. The ticket-scoped transient condition was cleared, allowing the already-running worker to retry the same durable message successfully. No worker restart, image redeployment, broker restart, database restart, or API restart was used.
